fatal_errors: The proposed graphene intervention is unrelated to the target intervention of varying Mo content in a CoCrFeNiMox-Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3 composite.
None of the cited evidence studies graphene-containing HEAs, graphene tribolayers, or wide-temperature self-lubrication, so it does not support the central mechanism or quantitative prediction.
The claim of improvement across the full temperature range is incompatible with the acknowledged risk of graphene oxidation and lacks a specified atmosphere or upper-temperature limit.
The asserted 20–40% improvement is not derived from any cited data.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the general goal of reducing friction and wear in an HEA and offers a controlled comparison with measurable falsification criteria. However, it does not reconstruct the target material, Mo-composition intervention, SPS conditions, phase evolution, or temperature-dependent MoS2/Ag and oxide–silver-molybdate lubrication mechanisms. Its baseline, graphene loading, processing route, temperature interval, load, speed, counterface, atmosphere, and sliding distance are unspecified. The experiment is directionally useful but insufficiently standardized to test a wide-temperature claim robustly. Most importantly, the supplied references concern HEA phase constitution, mechanical properties, or generic wear and provide no evidence for graphene dispersion, migration, tribolayer formation, or persistence at high temperature. Thus, the proposal is conceptually possible but unsupported as stated and cannot substantiate performance across the claimed service range.
